<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b18259ee85a2da8ed868c57a9a8ff8a64aee37d4` — the merge of head `b501462548d911695306ab278fbe7cca1d3b6e3e` into base `65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b18259ee85a2da8ed868c57a9a8ff8a64aee37d4 && git checkout b18259ee85a2da8ed868c57a9a8ff8a64aee37d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152 b501462548d911695306ab278fbe7cca1d3b6e3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152 && git merge --no-ff b501462548d911695306ab278fbe7cca1d3b6e3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 65ee4b7ad49361bc3cfaf3a32c9ed02752d4a152` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `805d6199124e63712dfc8e107cae8c50ed94206f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts + packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-index.ts, packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-object-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-provenance-stamp.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts; agreement only: packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json, packages/spec/liveness/object.json

Inputs read: card #32062 body and all 28 comments (through the slice-5 dev report 7118824246), PR #36795 body and both comments, the net diff `origin/main...805d6199`, the 70 check-runs on the head (60 success, 10 skipped, none failed), and on `origin/main`: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3, ADR-0153 D4 and its open points (the two this slice touches now sit at L853 and L854 of the file; the PR and the card cite them as L852 and L854).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Injected-columns plan (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`).** `plan.sync` is true for `managedBy: 'synced'` alone and false on both hard opt-outs (`systemFields: false`, `better-auth`); `names` gains the five columns under the same condition. Right: this is ADR-0153 D4's "on a `synced` object only". `InjectedSystemColumnPlan` gains a required `sync` member: a widening of a published return type; every in-repo constructor of the plan is this function. Right.
- **New public exports.** `SYNC_PROVENANCE_COLUMNS`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_PREFIX`, `SyncProvenanceColumn`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_FIELD_DEFS` from `@objectstack/spec/data`; `SYNC_PULL_WRITE`, `markSyncPullWrite`, `SyncProvenanceWriteRefusedError`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_WRITE_REFUSED_CODE` from `@objectstack/objectql`. All additions. `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each carry exactly the four spec names, with the right origins. Right.
- **Error-code ledger.** `ERR_SYNC_PROVENANCE_WRITE_REFUSED` is added under `@objectstack/objectql`, the package that throws it; the class carries `code`, `status: 400` and `httpStatus: 400` (ADR-0112). An addition to the accept-set of codes a client may receive. Right.
- **Registered shape of a synced object.** Five hidden, read-only, system columns and one index. The index is document-gated on `_sync_source` and `_sync_external_id` being present, which only the plan can cause on a parsed object (the prefix is reserved), and `applySystemFields` reaches the stamp only past the `!plan.sync` early return or with the columns already present. So it lands on synced objects only, led by `organization_id` when the object has the tenant column. Stamp order (after the tenant index) and strip order (before the tenant inverse) are consistent at both producers and in `stripMaterializedStampsFrom`. Right.
- **Write accept-set.** An insert or update whose payload names any key starting `_sync_` is refused on every object unless the context carries the pull's mark. All engine write doors funnel through the two guarded facets: `insert` (single and array), `insertMany` (calls `insert`), the repository `insert` / `create` / `update` / `updateById`, and `update` on both the by-id and the predicate exit. The refusal sits after `assertWriteAllowed` and before middleware, defaults and hooks. Right for the caller's payload; see S1 for what it does not judge.
- **Diagnostics.** `computeMetadataDiagnostics` leaves out a `_sync_` field only when it is identical to the platform definition (`isInjectedColumnDefinition`), so an authored `_sync_` field is still refused for the reserved prefix. Right, and it honours carrier note 6762989212 item 5.
- **Mapping refusal.** A `fieldMapping` target under `_sync_` is refused `400 mapping_target_refused` by both pulls before any read. It was refused before as an unknown target, so the author's accept-set does not move. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right. The engine now refuses a system-context write it used to judge like any other key, and the PR title carries `!`. The line is on the PR body and in the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No key, accepted value or metadata type is added, removed or re-shaped: the `_sync_` field prefix was reserved by #32118, a `_sync_` mapping target was already refused at run time, and the planned columns, the index and the error code are platform surface, not something an author writes. The new exports and the new code are a non-protocol widening.
- Level: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). The changeset moves the four packages the diff changes, each at `patch`. Right. The `Check Changeset` check-run is green on the head.
- Narrowing companions, all present: the BREAKING bullet states what is refused, with which code and status, and the one-line fix ("leave the `_sync_` columns out of the write; the next pull of the mapping stamps them"); exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which fits, since no authored value has to be rewritten; `Skills-docs: none` with its reason on both carriers, confirmed (no file under `skills/` or `ui/skills/` names `_sync_` or `SYNC_PROVENANCE` on the head); the dogfood battery on this head is in the dev report on the card (7118824246: `805d6199`, command-exit 0, 487 files passed, 3 skipped). The PR body's Verification section still reads "owed"; the reading exists, on the card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Composite `upsertKey` encoding (ADR-0153 open point "a composite `upsertKey` written as `_sync_external_id` text").** Answered in `encodeSyncExternalId`, cited at the spot in its doc comment, and pinned in `sync-provenance-stamp.test.ts` (single, composite, a value holding `","`, blanks) and through a real engine in `datasource-pull.test.ts` (`'["10","A-1"]'`). Judged in ④: it holds, with nits N1 to N3.
- **Two mappings on one target (ADR-0153 open point at L854).** Still open, as the claim's seat route requires: the diff adds no refusal of a second mapping on a target, in the spec files or in either pull. Each row carries `_sync_source`. See N4 for what slice 6 must weigh before it scopes a mark by that column.
- **`_sync_deleted_at` planned and unstamped (ADR-0078).** Allowed here: its field description says "Not written yet: the delete marking that stamps it has not landed, so it is empty on every row", the plan's doc comment says the same, and the `mapping.deletePolicy` liveness row (still `planned`) and the `object.managedBy` note both say it. The other four columns each have a writer in both pulls. `_sync_run_id` is left unwritten when no run ledger is composed, and its description says so.
- **`systemFields: false` on a synced target.** Not refused; the rows are written unstamped and unmarked, pinned in both pull tests and stated in `jobs.mdx`. Refusing it would narrow what an author may declare, which this slice does not claim. Left to D3, as the PR says. Accepted.
- **Dev report `open_questions`:** empty. Nothing to escalate to the maintainer.
- **SQL push-down:** no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The stamp is computed per row from values already in hand, and the index exists so that slice 6's diff can be a predicate.
- **Claim surface:** `metadata-diagnostics.ts` and the three one-sentence doc edits are outside the claimed file list and are declared as deviations with their reason. Without the diagnostics change every served synced object would read `valid: false`. Accepted.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts`** — against ADR-0153 D4 and its first consumer (`applySystemFields`, `syncProvenanceColumnAdditions`). The five names, the bucket condition and the opt-outs match the ADR table and the registry's injection. One sentence does not hold against the engine; see S1.

**`packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts`** — the five definitions are `hidden`, `readonly`, `system`, not required, text for the run id (never a lookup, as D7 requires), and `satisfies` ties them to the column list. `injectedSystemColumnDefs` follows `plan.sync`. The `_sync_deleted_at` description is truthful. "Written by the pull only." on the other four is the S1 sentence again. The `_sync_external_id` description is N2.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`** — the row agrees with `SyncProvenanceWriteRefusedError`: 400, judged on the caller's payload before middleware, defaults and hooks, system context included. The comment says "of a `synced` object"; the engine refuses the prefix on every object, which the reserved prefix makes equivalent in practice.

**Implementing files, against those contracts.**

- `sync-provenance-write.ts`, `engine-insert.ts`, `engine-update.ts`: the mark is a `Symbol.for` key that JSON cannot carry, it is consumed at the door (object rest keeps every other key, symbol keys included), and a hook's `ctx.api` write inside the pull's write is refused. Tests assert `code` and `status` for a system insert and a system update, the control write, the admitted pull write, the consumed mark and the nested hook write. The pull itself still writes: both pulls write under `markSyncPullWrite(context ?? { isSystem: true })`, pinned through a real engine.
- `sync-provenance-index.ts`, `registry.ts`, `registry-object-registration.ts`: hold, as in ①. The inverse is plan-gated and takes only an exact platform entry in last position; an author entry with a `name` stays.
- `sync-provenance-stamp.ts`: the encoding is injective over tuples of text (a JSON array of strings), order is the declared `upsertKey` order (both pulls pass `matchFields` in declaration order, unsorted), a blank part yields no id and the runner skips that row (`BLANK_MATCH_KEY`, any blank field in the key set), and arity is fixed within a mapping. A number and a string of the same digits spell alike; inside one key column of one type that cannot collide.
- `metadata-diagnostics.ts`: holds, as in ①.

**Findings.**

S1 (should-fix) — The published sentences say more than the engine enforces. `injected-system-columns.ts` says "The pull is the only writer of all five", `SYNC_PROVENANCE_FIELD_DEFS` says "Written by the pull only." on four columns, the changeset title says "nothing else may write those columns", and `jobs.mdx` says "Nothing else writes these columns". ADR-0153 D4 says "A `_sync_` column in any write except the pull's is refused by name, whatever the caller's context" and "the pull is their only writer". `refuseSyncProvenanceWrite` judges the caller's payload only, before the hooks run. A `beforeInsert` or `beforeUpdate` hook on a synced object that assigns a `_sync_` key to the write's data is not judged: on a system write the static `readonly` strip is skipped, and a hook-assigned key is exempt from it in any case (`hookWrittenKeys`), so the value reaches the driver. That covers a declared action's system write and the pull's own write, where a hook can replace `_sync_source` or set `_sync_deleted_at`, the two columns slice 6's mark reads. The PR body discloses this under "What the refusal judges"; no published sentence does. Either judge the post-hook write image too (the engine already tracks hook-written keys per row on insert, and the update door has the same seam), with a test for a hook that assigns a `_sync_` key on a system write and on the pull's write; or, if the seat keeps the payload-only rule, say so in the four sentences above and record the deviation from D4's letter on the card for slice 6.

S2 (should-fix) — The connector pull decides whether to stamp from a schema read that fails open. In `connector-pull.ts` the target's definition is read inside `try { … } catch { }`; when that read throws or answers nothing, `carriesSyncProvenanceColumns(undefined)` is false, so the rows of a synced target are written with no `_sync_` column and no mark, and nothing is logged or refused. The changeset and `jobs.mdx` both say every row a pull writes gets the four stamps. The datasource pull has no such path: it refuses before the first read unless the target is known and `synced`. An unstamped row carries no `_sync_source`, so slice 6 can never mark it, and an incremental pull never reads it again to repair it. Make the connector pull refuse the run (or otherwise not write) when a sourced mapping's target definition cannot be read, with a test; or state the exception where the two sentences are published.

N1 — `encodeSyncExternalId`'s comment gives "two fields' values are not interchangeable" as the reason not to sort. Sorting by field name would not interchange values; the real property is that the order is the author's declaration. A reordered `upsertKey` therefore re-keys every row the next run writes, and rows that run does not read keep the old spelling until a complete read. D3's completeness rule bounds the harm, since a mark needs a complete read, which restamps every live row. Carry to slice 6: its diff must not compare ids across a changed `upsertKey` before a complete read.

N2 — ADR-0153's table defines `_sync_external_id` as "the source values `upsertKey`'s target fields are copied from, as text". The stamp reads the mapped row (`row[f]` after `applyMappingToRows`), so for any transform other than a plain copy or a lookup it is the transformed value, not the source value. The column description ("the source value of the mapping's upsertKey") follows the ADR's wording, not the code. The PR body discloses it. Slice 6 computes its diff from the same mapped rows, so the two sides agree; align the description, or record the deviation, when the file is next touched.

N3 — Spelling edges the tests do not pin, none reachable inside one well-typed key column: an object key part is spelled with `JSON.stringify`, whose member order is not canonical; a `Date` part is cut to milliseconds; a decimal that one driver returns as the number `1.1` and another as the string `"1.10"` spells two ways.

N4 — `_sync_source` holds the mapping's bare name, as the ADR table says. Slice 3's finding (record 6786503520, S1) established that a mapping's identity is its holder package plus its name: two packages may each hold a mapping of one name. If both write one target, their rows carry one `_sync_source`. That is the L854 case with no way to tell the writers apart. Carry to slice 6 before a mark is scoped by this column.

N5 — `markSyncPullWrite` and `SYNC_PULL_WRITE` are public exports of `@objectstack/objectql`, and the mark is a `Symbol.for` key, so any in-process code can mint it. "Only the pull calls it" is a convention, not an enforced rule. In-process code is trusted today; the export's comment could say so.

N6 — The refusal tests pin a single-row system insert and a by-id system update. An array insert, `insertMany` and a predicate update are covered by construction (one funnel each) but have no pin of their own.

N7 — The PR body's Verification section still says the dogfood battery is owed, and the PR and the card cite the composite-key open point as L852; it is at L853 of the ADR on `main`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-l53erx`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufziwMkZG34d69p8BHb4`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 805d6199 · 2026-11-24T01:21Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `805d6199124e63712dfc8e107cae8c50ed94206f`
Card: #32062, slice 5 (route A, the D4 column half) · claim 7101769273 · os-dev-report 7118824246.
Contract review on this head: 7119012685 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, PASS with two open should-fix findings; claim 7118910439).

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` at this head. Draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #32062`. Slice 6 (D3 + N1–N5) is still owed on the card, so `Part of` is right and no closing keyword binds any card. `pm:dispatched` stays on the card until slice 6 lands.
- **Checks at this head:** 70 check-runs. 60 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check: success. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges`: NOT governed, 0 of 34 paths, 1313 lines. Tier H comes from the narrowing leg, as the seat said.
- **Narrowing companions:**
  - The `!` in the title and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` appear in the body and the changeset.
  - The changeset carries a BREAKING bullet with its fix ("leave the `_sync_` columns out of the write; the next pull stamps them") and one ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker.
  - `Skills-docs: none`: confirmed, nothing under `skills/**` names `_sync_`, `managedBy: 'synced'` or `SYNC_PROVENANCE`.
  - Dogfood battery on `805d6199`: os-verify-lock VERDICT exit 0, 487 files passed and 3 skipped, 4125 tests passed and 68 skipped (report 7118824246). Full, pinned to this head.
- **Declarations:** `Metadata-protocol: none` and patch on all four packages. The contract review's ② agrees: the planned columns, the index, the exports and the new error code change nothing an author writes. The changeset names every published package whose `src/**` moved: spec, objectql, metadata-protocol and service-automation.
- **Scope vs claim:** these files sit outside the claim's surface:
  - `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`: the new code's ledger row, which ADR-0112 requires for a new wire code;
  - `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts`: the field definitions the plan rows inject;
  - `metadata-protocol` diagnostics and their test, the one non-sync-in docs sentence each in `objects.mdx`, `hooks.mdx` and `flows.mdx`, and the reader-ledger row in `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`. The report declares all of these.
  - generated references and baselines.

  Each is a direct consequence of the claimed change. The two spec files are not in the report's `deviations` list, so the seat should amend the claim's `File surface:` line with them (paper).
- **Tests:** real commands with output. The ablation disabled the throw, three refusal cases went red and the restore went green. The refusal cases assert `code` (`SYNC_PROVENANCE_WRITE_REFUSED_CODE`) and `status` 400 for a system insert, a system update and a hook's `ctx.api` write (ADR-0112). There is a CONTROL for a plain system write, and the marked pull write is admitted with its mark consumed. Overlap with #36796 is clean on `engine-insert.ts` and `engine-update.ts`.
- **Docs, read sentence by sentence:**
  - `jobs.mdx` "Every row says where it came from": five columns, the index, four stamps, the composite encoding with its example, `_sync_deleted_at` empty, the refusal with its code, the `fieldMapping` refusal and `systemFields: false`. Each matches the code, except "Nothing else writes these columns" and "every row a pull writes gets", which are S1 and S2.
  - `objects.mdx` table cell, and the `hooks.mdx` / `flows.mdx` null-guard sentences (`_sync_deleted_at` always null for now): true.
  - `references/api/*` and `error-code-ledger.mdx`: generated, +1 code each.
  - Changeset bullets 1–4 read against the diff; they carry the same two gaps.

### Findings
**Should-fix** (both are the contract review's; I re-read each in the code):
- **S1 (should-fix)** = contract review S1.
  - `refuseSyncProvenanceWrite` judges the caller's payload before the hooks run.
  - A `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate` hook that assigns a `_sync_` key on a system write is not judged. That includes the pull's own write, where a hook could replace `_sync_source` or set `_sync_deleted_at`, the two columns slice 6 reads. Hook-written keys are exempt from the readonly strip, so the value reaches the driver.
  - ADR-0153 D4 and four published sentences say the pull is the only writer: `injected-system-columns.ts`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_FIELD_DEFS` ("Written by the pull only."), the changeset title, and `jobs.mdx`.
  - Fix: judge the post-hook write image too, with tests for a hook on a system write and on the pull's write. Alternatively, if payload-only is kept, soften the four sentences and record the deviation on the card for slice 6.
- **S2 (should-fix)** = contract review S2.
  - `connector-pull.ts:771-778` reads the target definition inside `try { … } catch { }`.
  - If that read throws or answers nothing, `carriesSyncProvenanceColumns(undefined)` is false, and a synced target's rows are written unstamped, unmarked and unlogged.
  - Such rows have no `_sync_source`, so slice 6 can never mark them. The changeset and `jobs.mdx` say every row a pull writes gets the four stamps. The datasource pull refuses instead.
  - Fix: refuse the run (no write) when a sourced mapping's target definition cannot be read, with a test, or state the exception where those sentences are published. Refusing is the reading the docs imply.

**Nits** (the contract review's N1–N7, with no effect on correctness or the contract this slice):
